record.paper_title: The origin and evolution of transition discs: successes, problems and open questions
record.original_question: What is the true gas structure and kinematics inside mm-bright transition-disc cavities, and how should the currently observed gas density drops and inner-cavity gas detections be reconciled into a single physical picture?

evidence.quote: It is not clear how this fits into the entire picture yet as gas has only been imaged in a few cases and the interpretation is not without problems as we will discuss in Section-4.
However, there are still a few outstanding issues, particularly with regard to the structure and kinematics of the gas component

artifact.status_search_result: The question of the gas structure, kinematics, and clearing mechanism inside transition-disc cavities remains an active open problem. Reviews and ALMA-era studies subsequent to 2015 (e.g., Andrews 2020 ARA&A; van der Marel et al. 2016, 2021; Francis & van der Marel 2020; Facchini et al. 2018) characterize gas drops and kinematic signatures in individual sources but no single unified model accounts for all mm-bright transition discs; multiple mechanisms (planet-disc interaction, photoevaporation, MHD winds, dead zones) remain under debate.

status_evidence.title: Structures in Protoplanetary Disks (Andrews 2020, ARA&A)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews ALMA observations of transition disc cavities, noting persistent uncertainty in gas content, kinematics, and clearing mechanism.
status_evidence.claim: The origin of the gas/dust structure of transition disc cavities remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: van der Marel et al. 2016, A&A 585, A58 — Resolved gas cavities in transitional disks
status_evidence.snippet: Models gas surface density drops of 10–10^4 inside dust cavities; finds drops smaller than for dust, consistent with planet-induced clearing but not uniquely so.
status_evidence.claim: Inner-cavity gas drops are measured but the responsible mechanism is not uniquely determined.
